headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP plus broad egress in a closed-source/open-source pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files and call MCP, while Windsurf can use MCP and shares state via local filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from A can reach B’s instruction parser. The pathway is not proven by sandbox evidence, so I avoid high, but the shared surfaces make injection realistic.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes research output into a workspace file that Windsurf later opens
IF either agent treats file or MCP content as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the agents
Route A’s outputs through a plain-text sanitizer before B reads them
Require provenance labels on MCP/file content
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf
requires-engineering: add content-isolation between agent outputs and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress; B reads and writes workspace files and also has broad egress. In a shared filesystem setup, sensitive content can flow from A into B and then out through B’s model proxy or MCP calls. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without special setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or synced files
IF A ingests local documents containing secrets or personal data
IF B forwards workspace content to external model or MCP services
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict A to non-sensitive inputs only
Disable B’s access to files produced by A
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem and modify git state, while gpt-researcher can read files and run subprocesses with multiple instances supported. Because B explicitly shares state via local filesystem, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide with A’s file reads and generated artifacts. The overlap is dangerous by default in shared repos.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace
IF B auto-saves or auto-commits while A is generating files
IF A and B run concurrently in separate instances
mitigations: Use separate git branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable auto-commit or auto-save in Windsurf
Keep A read-only when B is editing
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared repositories

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a research/content-writing agent that produces citations and reports, and Windsurf is a coding agent that can act on workspace content. If B treats A’s generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or shell actions. No verification mechanism is shown, so I choose high over medium due to the action-taking potential.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses gpt-researcher output as source-of-truth without independent verification
IF A’s report contains hallucinated facts or citations
IF B converts that report into code changes, commits, or shell commands
mitigations: Require manual review of A’s outputs before B acts
Ask B to verify claims against primary sources
Disable direct handoff from A reports into B tasks
Limit B to read-only analysis for A-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add structured verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles local documents, citations, and images, while B handles workspace files and can transmit content via broad egress. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or secrets enters the shared workspace
IF either agent sends that data to external model providers or APIs
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use separate tenants or accounts
Review retention settings for both tools
Document allowed data classes per agent
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
